transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Thank you. Um, well, I'm mainly here because my sleep has just gotten really unreliable lately. It's like, even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there replaying sales forecasts and team issues in my head. And then I usually end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again.
Aside from feeling exhausted, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I get frustrated because I'm so tired all the time, and I'm definitely stressed about work, but I don't feel sad or hopeless. It's really just that I can't seem to shut my mind off, rather than feeling down.
Aside from work, do you find yourself worrying about other areas of your life, such as family, health, or everyday matters?

Yeah, I do. It's not just work, though work is a big part of it. Most days, my mind just kind of jumps around. Like, I'll be worrying about whether we'll hit our launch numbers, and then I'll start thinking about whether someone on my team is unhappy and about to quit. But then it bleeds into other stuff, too, like paying the mortgage or whether a client is going to renew their contract. It just feels like any little delay or hiccup could turn into a major disaster, and I can't stop thinking about all the things that could go wrong.
How long have you been dealing with this kind of constant worrying?

Well, it hasn't always been this bad, but... I'd say it's been building up for a while now. Probably since we had a big reorganization in the sales division at work. That was about thirteen months ago, and it feels like the worrying just kind of started then and never really stopped.
Have you noticed any physical tension in your body, like tight muscles, aches, or soreness?

Yeah, definitely. I just feel wound up almost all the time, honestly. It's like... well, it's like I'm sitting in a stressful pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And my shoulders really take the brunt of it. They just stay tight no matter how much I try to relax them.
